sections.summary: Added a two-lane admission semaphore to gitCommands.ts: MAX_CONCURRENT_COMMANDS = max(4, cpus-2) (8 on this 10-core machine) with MAX_BACKGROUND_COMMANDS = max(1, limit-2) = 6, so two slots are permanently reserved for the interactive lane. runCommand gained a 7th positional parameter `lane: CommandLane = 'interactive'`, awaits `commandSemaphore.acquire(lane, signal)` and releases in a finally; the previous body is now the private `spawnCommand()`. Waiting interactive commands are always admitted before waiting background ones, a waiter whose AbortSignal fires leaves the queue and rejects with COMMAND_ABORTED_MESSAGE instead of spawning when its turn arrives, and the release closure is idempotent. Lane priority alone only orders the queue, which is why the background reservation is there: without it a burst of remote probes that had already filled every slot would still make the next interactive command wait for a child to exit, which is exactly the measured Cmd+H failure. Callers marked background: the gitignored listing (`#startIgnoredListing` passes 'background' through a new optional third parameter on `#git`) and the non-open-root `git remote -v` probe in `remotesForRoot`. GitObjectReader deliberately still bypasses the semaphore — its long-lived `cat-file --batch` child would hold a slot for its whole 60 s idle window. searchContent spawns ripgrep with `spawn()` directly, not through runCommand, so it is not admitted (and is interactive anyway).

sections.deviations: The background reservation (MAX_BACKGROUND_COMMANDS) is beyond the literal plan text, which only asked for lane priority in the queue. It is the part that actually bounds interactive latency during a probe burst, and it is documented in the source. `lane` was added as a 7th positional parameter rather than an options bag, to match the existing positional signature and avoid touching 20 call sites.

sections.summary: Verified first, then fixed. Evidence: vendor-shiki (206,721 B) was statically imported by vendor-diffs, which the viewer chunks import statically — so its module body was fetched, parsed and evaluated before the workspace painted, not merely referenced. Per-module minified attribution from the source map: @shikijs/vscode-textmate 42.5 KB, oniguruma-to-es + oniguruma-parser + regex* ~56 KB, @shikijs/core 18 KB, @shikijs/primitive 13.5 KB, engine-oniguruma 7 KB. The app already highlights in a worker (DIFF_WORKER_POOL_OPTIONS -> @pierre/diffs/worker/worker.js); FileRenderer.js:132 only builds a main-thread highlighter when the worker pool has failed or an edit session is attached, and nothing in src/renderer calls preloadHighlighter/getSharedHighlighter/FileStream. Four static edges held the engine on the boot path and all four are now gone: (1) a renderer-only build plugin rewrites @pierre/diffs shared_highlighter.js so the engine import happens inside the already-async getSharedHighlighter; (2) a second plugin does the same for normalizeTheme inside @pierre/theming createTheme's async loader; (3) @pierre/diffs/dist/edit|editor got its own manual chunk so the editor's `shiki/textmate` import stops riding vendor-diffs; (4) shiki/dist/langs-bundle-full got an explicit chunk name so Rollup could not merge it back into the engine, and @shikijs/transformers was left unassigned so it inlines next to its importer. A new vendor-hast chunk holds the HTML serializer shared by markdown, the highlighter and FileRenderer.renderPartialHTML. Result: vendor-shiki (143,344 B) is now imported only dynamically by vendor-diffs and statically by vendor-diffs-edit, which is itself off the pre-mount path. Pre-mount closure 1,652,620 -> 1,361,302 B at the end of this section. Both plugins throw a named build error if the vendored anchor text drifts. The worker bundle is untouched (207,921 B, still bundling textmate and oniguruma-to-es eagerly), so worker highlight latency is unchanged; the only path that now pays an extra 143 KB warm file:// chunk fetch is attaching an editor to an already-painted file, or a worker-pool failure, both already async.

Two @pierre/* modules are rewritten at build time, which the plan flagged as a possible blocker — it is not a blocker here because the repo already does exactly this for shiki themes (trimShikiThemesPlugin) and shiki/wasm (dropShikiWasmPlugin), both rewrites are inside functions that are already async, and both fail the build loudly if the anchors move. No named `vendor-shiki absent` assertion was added to check-entry-chunk.mjs because the brief scopes that file to ratchet-only; the ratcheted byte budget is what catches a regression.

sections.summary: Three deliverables, two fully met and one short of its number. (1) Split: styles.css 203,745 -> 98,151 source bytes; built boot CSS 172,331 -> 79,773 B (-53.7%), against a target of < 60,000. Ten per-component sheets now ship with their chunks — AgentPanel 19,267, PerformanceHud 16,949, MultiFileReview 14,516, GitHubPanel 13,775, SettingsPage 10,840, TerminalDock 7,360, GitHubMarkdownRenderer 3,969, and ReviewComments + PullRequestReviewBar + PullRequestContext folded into the viewer chunk's 8,293 B sheet. A rule moved only when every comma-separated selector had a leading compound belonging to one surface; @media/@container/@starting-style blocks were partitioned the same way and each moved partition appended after that surface's base rules, so cross-cutting overrides (the 3,867 B prefers-reduced-motion block spans six surfaces) still win. An audit of every moved class against the nine boot-chunk components sent five groups back to styles.css — the pull request loading indicator, .review-locator, .editor-option-controls, .markdown-view-toggle and .github-markdown-fallback are painted by boot components before their surface's chunk exists. The command palette, .agent-dock*, folder picker, world strip, app shell, explorer and diff container were deliberately left in the boot sheet for the same reason. 60 KB is not reachable without moving the explorer/app-shell rules the cached first paint uses: the remaining sheet is tokens (4.3 KB), resets, cross-cutting @media (6.5 KB) and boot-path chrome, and the only movable remainder is ~6.6 KB of viewer-internal rules that would land at ~74 KB. (2) Squircle: the universal rule was split so `corner-shape: squircle` no longer resolves against `*::before, *::after`; the nine pseudo-element rules that set a border-radius and relied on it now declare it themselves, and the three that sit in the `corner-shape: round` opt-out list were left alone because a later squircle declaration would have beaten the opt-out and turned true circles into rounded squares. (3) SidebarResizer: RB-12's 'read layout once on pointerdown' was already implemented and already covered by the existing dom test (verified, no change needed). The transform-during-drag half was not implemented — the sidebar width is the grid track, so a transform-only drag turns live resizing into a ghost divider that snaps on release, a UX regression I cannot visually validate. Instead the two real remaining costs went: a pointermove that rounds to the same pixel no longer writes --sidebar-width at all, and committing no longer measures and writes a second time (every commit path writes through commitWidth and records the painted width; the layout effect returns early when the DOM already carries it). getBoundingClientRect is now read once per drag, once per keystroke and once on mount.

reviewNotes:
RISKY SPOTS, in order of how much I would want a second pair of eyes on them.

1. The two build-time rewrites of vendored modules (electron.vite.config.ts). horus:lazy-highlighter-engine moves @pierre/diffs shared_highlighter.js's `import { createHighlighter, createJavaScriptRegexEngine, createOnigurumaEngine } from "shiki"` inside the already-async getSharedHighlighter; horus:lazy-theme-normalizer does the same for `normalizeTheme` inside @pierre/theming normalizingLoader's async arrow. Both preserve semantics — the `highlighter ??= createHighlighter(...)` assignment is still synchronous within one microtask resumption, so two concurrent callers still share one instance — but the synchronous exports (isHighlighterLoaded, getHighlighterIfLoaded, isHighlighterNull) now report "not loaded" for the extra ticks it takes the chunk to arrive. Nothing in src/renderer reads them; @pierre/diffs reads them only on the main-thread fallback path, where the effect is that a file renders plain for a few extra ms before the highlight lands. Both plugins are renderer-only and throw a named error if the anchors drift; scripts/lazyHighlighter.test.mjs asserts the anchors at bun test time so a dependency bump names itself.

2. CSS cascade after the split. Rules moved out land in a stylesheet that loads after boot.css, so anything in styles.css that used to override them with equal specificity would now lose. I mitigated this by only moving rules whose selectors ALL belong to one surface, and by partitioning cross-cutting @media/@container/@starting-style blocks and appending each partition after that surface's base rules in the same file. The five groups a boot component paints before its surface's chunk exists (pull request loading indicator, .review-locator, .editor-option-controls, .markdown-view-toggle, .github-markdown-fallback) were returned to styles.css, but appended at the END of the file rather than at their original positions — their original offsets were gone by then. These are uniquely-named surfaces so I do not expect a precedence change, but it is the one place where cascade order genuinely moved. I could not launch the app, so nothing here is visually verified.

3. Squircle scoping. I removed `*::before, *::after` from the corner-shape rule and gave the nine pseudo-element rules that set a border-radius their own declaration — except the three that appear in the `corner-shape: round` opt-out list (.performance-live > span::before, .performance-chart-tooltip dt::before, .file-edit-state::before). Adding squircle to those would have beaten the earlier opt-out and turned three true circles into rounded squares; I caught it on the first pass and reverted them. Worth re-checking that no other pseudo-element in the app relies on the removed global.

4. SidebarResizer: I did not implement transform-during-drag. The sidebar width IS the grid track, so a transform-only drag decouples the divider from the panel and the layout snaps on release — a real UX downgrade I cannot validate visually. If Fable wants the ghost divider anyway it is a small change on top of what is there. What I did instead removes a per-frame style write on high-rate pointers and one measure+write per commit. RB-12's "read layout once on pointerdown" was already true before this wave and already covered by a test dated 31 Aug.

5. Deliberately NOT split out of boot.css, all for the same reason — a boot-chunk component paints them before the owning chunk exists: the command palette (CommandPaletteHost renders the .command-palette-layer / .command-palette / .command-palette-results shell from boot, and P14/P18 specifically tuned that first frame — 3.6 KB was not worth an unstyled first Cmd+P), .agent-dock* (AgentDock's Suspense fallback), the folder picker, world strip, app shell, explorer and diff container.

THINGS I COULD NOT VERIFY. Anything requiring a running app: no visual check of the split stylesheets, no first-highlight latency measurement, no git-shim spawn counts for the semaphore. The 100 ms first-highlight criterion for P31 is reasoned, not measured: every diff and file view highlights in the worker, whose bundle is byte-for-byte unchanged in structure (207,921 B, textmate and oniguruma-to-es still eager, only shiki/wasm dynamic), so the first highlighted file cannot have regressed. The paths that now pay one extra warm 143 KB file:// chunk fetch are attaching an editor to a file that is already on screen, and a worker-pool failure.

BASELINE CAVEAT. The "before" build I measured at the start of this session already contained Waves 1-2 plus whatever Tracks C/D/E had written by then, and they kept editing boot-chunk source throughout. The +5,659 B on the boot chunk is theirs; the closure and CSS numbers are mine.

TWO SMALL SUGGESTIONS FOR THE OWNER OF scripts/check-entry-chunk.mjs (ratchet-only for me): add a `vendor-shiki absent from the pre-mount closure` assertion next to the existing `WorkerPool absent from boot` one, so a re-import of the engine names itself instead of just tripping the byte budget; and consider printing boot CSS bytes there too, since P30's target is stated in those terms and nothing currently measures it automatically.
